title: I'm building a browser game where you run a security operations centre and fend off (or launch) hacking raids. Looking for pre-alpha testers
author: Plastic-Sugar1680
selftext:
Hey all,



I've been building a game called Project C, and I'm after a few dozen people to break it before it goes any wider.



The idea: you run a small security operations centre (SOC) in a living world. You have a 3D control room, a watchtower, a map of the world, and a terminal. You earn credits, level up and pick perks.



You can play both sides:



\- \*\*Defend:\*\* alerts come in and you work out which ones are real. You write detection rules and decide whether to isolate a system, reset credentials or just sit back and watch the attacker. Watching teaches you the most but can cost you.

\- \*\*Attack:\*\* you plan a raid against other players or the resident bots: recon, break in, move sideways, then go for the goal. It takes real time and costs energy, so you need to pick your moments.



A few things I'm pleased with:



\- A world full of resident bots that attack each other, so something is always happening on the map, even when it's quiet.

\- An attack tree that shows how far along you are and where you can go next, based on how real intrusions work, simplified to be fun.

\- It's a game with simulated targets. Nothing in it touches real systems, and you don't need any security background.



It's pre-alpha, so expect rough edges. I'm after honest feedback on whether the first hour is fun, what's confusing and where it gets boring. Early players have already told me level 1 to 2 felt slow, so that's been reworked.



If you want in, comment or message me, or join the Discord: [https://discord.gg/nTbVdN5pd](https://discord.gg/nTbVdN5pd)



Happy to answer anything about how it works.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Plastic-Sugar1680 please add details on how AI was used to make this. Just stating that you used AI doesn't pass the rule. The community is a dev community, add dev details. Rule 4 is there to make sure promotional posts contribute by getting into the process and actual development. There's a real risk of the sub being swamped by self-promotion. If you don't update, this post may be removed.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body:
Please see the requirements for posts about commercial games promotion.

**Game Promotion Posts Allowed, with Requirements**

You must discuss your game within the context of how it was developed using AI. Share with the community and give something for the community to talk about in your development experience with AI. A fire and forget video/image with no text, chatGPT bullet list may be removed by mods. If your game is being sold, you MUST apply the "Commercial Self Promotion" flair.
